issues.legal_issue: An award granting property to a woman as its permanent owner confers an absolute estate when its operative words are clear and the other passages do not unambiguously qualify them.
material_facts: The award allotted the disputed properties to a daughter and described each recipient as the permanent owner of the allotted share.
Other passages in the award referred to the nature of the properties, the arbitrator’s view of inheritance, and a possible later devolution to the daughter’s son.
Those passages did not unambiguously qualify the operative grant.
issues.conclusion: The award granted the daughter an absolute estate in the disputed properties.
issues.legal_principle: A document must be construed according to its clear operative language; surrounding passages do not qualify that language unless they do so unambiguously. The Court relied on Ram Gopal v. Nand Lal (1950) S.C.R. 766 at 778 and Bishunath Prasad Singh v. Chandika Prasad Kumari (1933) 60 I.A. 56 at 61–62.

predicates.award_interpretation_case: The court is deciding the meaning of an award or comparable written instrument.
predicates.operative_words_confer_permanent_ownersh: The instrument’s operative words describe the recipient as the permanent owner of the property allotted to that recipient.
predicates.surrounding_passages_do_not_unambiguousl: Other passages in the instrument do not clearly and unambiguously limit the ownership stated in its operative words.

issues.definition: When an award is being interpreted, its operative words confer absolute ownership if they state permanent ownership and the surrounding passages do not unambiguously qualify that grant.

issues.legal_issue: A person who accepts a division of disputed property, induces the other claimant to rely on that acceptance to their detriment, and obtains a benefit from it is estopped from later denying the represented facts underlying the other claimant’s title.
material_facts: A claimant seriously asserted a right to the whole estate, while the daughter asserted a right to separate and exclusive possession and to an absolute share.
After the dispute was referred to arbitration and an award divided the estate, the parties accepted the division and acted on it rather than continuing their dispute.
The claimant retained property allotted to him, while the daughter gave up an appreciable portion of the estate and relied on the claimant’s acceptance of her absolute title to her allotment.
The claimant retained the benefit of the division and did not attempt to undo it during his lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was estopped from denying the facts that, as recognized through his acceptance of the division, gave the daughter an absolute interest in her allotted properties; the award’s validity or binding effect was not necessary to that conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Estoppel requires a representation of existing fact, reliance on that representation that induces action, and resulting detriment. Although estoppel does not arise merely on a question of law, conduct may represent an admission of the facts that produce a legal consequence. A party may accept and act on a division even if the underlying award could be challenged. The Court relied on Kanhai Lal v. Brij Lal (1919) 45 I.A. 118 and distinguished the question of estoppel from the validity or binding force of the award itself.

rule.if: property_dispute_case and claimant_accepted_property_division and acceptance_represented_existing_facts and other_claimant_relied_and_suffered_detriment and accepting_claimant_received_benefit

predicates.property_dispute_case: The proceeding concerns competing claims to property divided between claimants.
predicates.claimant_accepted_property_division: A claimant accepted and acted on a division of the disputed property instead of pursuing the dispute further.
predicates.acceptance_represented_existing_facts: The claimant’s acceptance represented recognition of existing facts underlying the other claimant’s asserted title.
predicates.other_claimant_relied_and_suffered_detri: The other claimant relied on that acceptance and gave up property or otherwise changed position to their detriment.
predicates.accepting_claimant_received_benefit: The claimant who accepted the division retained or obtained a benefit from it.

issues.definition: In a property dispute, a claimant is estopped from denial when that claimant accepts a division in a way that represents existing facts, the other claimant relies on it to their detriment, and the accepting claimant receives a benefit.

issues.legal_issue: A presumptive reversioner who knowingly takes and retains property solely under a division accepted by an earlier holder is estopped from later challenging that division when the reversion opens, including when claiming in the new capacity of reversioner.
material_facts: The son had no independent title to the property allotted to his father when he took possession after his father’s death; he claimed through his father.
He knew of the award and the division made under it, took possession with his brother, and dealt with the property as their own for many years.
He benefited from the property and did not object while the daughter treated her own allotment as absolute property, including when she gifted it to her grandsons.
After the daughter’s son died, the son became the presumptive reversioner, and the reversion opened while the son was alive.
issues.conclusion: The son was estopped both through his father and by his own conduct, and the estoppel continued after the reversion opened despite his claim in the character of reversioner.
issues.legal_principle: An estoppel may bind a successor who takes through the person estopped, and a person who knowingly accepts and benefits from a transaction may be precluded from challenging it even when later claiming in a different capacity. A reversioner who personally consented to and benefited from a transaction may remain estopped when the reversion opens. The Court relied on Kanhai Lal v. Brij Lal (1919) 45 I.A. 118 and Ramgouda Annagouda v. Bhausaheb (1927) 54 I.A. 396 at 403; it distinguished Rangasami Gounden v. Nachiappa Gounden (1919) 46 I.A. 72 and Mt. Binda Kuer v. Lalitha Prasad on the facts concerning independent title and benefit.

rule.if: reversionary_succession_case and claimant_took_only_through_estopped_predecessor and claimant_knew_of_division and claimant_retained_and_benefited_from_property_under_division and claimant_later_claimed_as_reversioner

predicates.reversionary_succession_case: The proceeding concerns a claim to property after a limited holder’s estate ends and the reversion opens.
predicates.claimant_took_only_through_estopped_pred: The claimant acquired possession or asserted title through a predecessor who was estopped from challenging the division.
predicates.claimant_knew_of_division: The claimant knew of the division under which the property was held.
predicates.claimant_retained_and_benefited_from_pro: The claimant retained and derived benefit from the property on the basis of the division.
predicates.claimant_later_claimed_as_reversioner: The claimant later asserted a right to the property in the capacity of reversioner.

issues.definition: A claimant remains estopped as a reversioner when, in a reversionary succession case, the claimant took only through an estopped predecessor, knew of the division, retained and benefited from property under it, and later claimed as reversioner.

issues.legal_issue: Persons claiming through a reversioner who remains estopped are themselves estopped from asserting the claim that the reversioner could not pursue.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed through the son who had taken and retained the property under the division and was estopped from challenging it even after the reversion opened.
The parties accepted that if the son remained estopped after the reversion opened, the plaintiffs claiming through him were also estopped.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were estopped from pursuing their claim through the son.
issues.legal_principle: A person claiming through an individual who remains estopped is bound by that estoppel. The Court applied the parties’ concession concerning the effect of the estoppel against the son.

predicates.claimant_derivative_rights_case: The proceeding concerns a claim asserted through another person rather than on an independent title.
predicates.predecessor_remains_estopped: The person through whom the claim is made remains estopped from asserting the disputed right.
predicates.claimant_asserts_right_through_predecess: The claimant bases the disputed claim on a right derived through that person.

issues.definition: A claimant is estopped when the claim is derivative and the person through whom it is asserted remains estopped.
